name: Firstsource Solutions Ltd
title: Firstsource Solutions Ltd - 532809 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Firstsource raised FY27 constant-currency revenue floor to 10.5% (from 10%) and reaffirmed 12.25–12.75% EBIT margin; no supply-side or capex signal, growth and margin story is management-led with H2 back-loading.

summary.headline: Firstsource Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR 28.3bn (12.3% constant currency), EBIT margin 12.5%; FY27 CC revenue guidance floor raised to 10.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 3.7% QoQ in INR and 2% QoQ in constant currency, the 12th straight quarter of sequential growth, with EBIT margin at 12.5% (up 100 bps YoY, 10 bps QoQ) for an eighth straight quarter of expansion. Management signed four large deals (two from new logos) and added 17 new logos, including six strategic logos. Headcount rose by 3,062 to 39,937, largely from a major banking client transition and offshore/nearshore ramps. FY27 constant currency revenue guidance was narrowed upward to 10.5%-13% from 10%-13%, with the EBIT margin guidance of 12.25%-12.75% reaffirmed. Healthcare declined 2% QoQ, and the company is still pursuing recovery on the exceptional charge tied to two clients from last quarter.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 17.1 billion at end June 2026

segments.name: Banking & Financial Services (BFS)
segments.commentary: Grew 19% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency, with nine new logos; growth broad-based and led North America and Europe. Management said it would not read anything into a slight dip in BFS margin on a quarterly basis.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY but declined 2% QoQ in constant currency (Q1 was +11% YoY), with four new logos. Management attributed the softness to Medicare Advantage scope recalibration after CMS rate changes and the wind-down of a transformative payer BPaaS engagement.

segments.name: Communications, Media & Technology (CMT)
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, with two new logos; management flagged quarter-to-quarter volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions.

segments.name: Utilities & Retail
segments.commentary: Grew 25% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, with two new logos; retail seasonal ramps expected in Q3 and part of Q4.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and 1% QoQ in constant currency; BFS led growth while healthcare reflected program ramp timing.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY and 7% QoQ in constant currency, led by BFS with CMT momentum; two large wins in the quarter.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 50% YoY, supported by existing relationships and an improving pipeline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guidance raised at the lower end to 10.5%-13% (earlier 10%-13%); upper end of 13% kept 'very much in play', dependent on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance reaffirmed at 12.25%-12.75%.
Management expects a 50-75 bps annual margin improvement to continue over the next couple of years, targeting a 14%-15% EBIT margin band within two to three years.
FY27 effective tax rate guided at 22%-24%.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1, citing large-deal ramps, the banking client transition, 17 new logos, and a healthy pipeline described as the best ever.

Wage increments: frontline and mid-level staff received hikes in Q2, senior staff in Q3; management said forecasts already reflect this and remain within guidance. Quantification was deferred to an offline follow-up.
capex_capacity: Headcount closed Q2 at 39,937, net addition of 3,062 QoQ; India and Philippines accounted for more than 85% of the increase, with South Africa also contributing.
About 80% of gross hiring is offshore or nearshore; onboarding of around 3,000 people was largely ahead of revenue for the banking client transition.

Kairos platform capitalisation is work in progress; some directly attributable costs are capitalised. Intangible asset under development was INR 232 million; the capitalised Kairos cost figure was to be provided offline.

M&A philosophy: plug capability gaps (healthcare, retail, distribution access). Past deals cited: QBSS (~3 years ago, RCM mid-office), Ascensos (retail, ~2 years ago), TeleMedik (earlier in FY27, Puerto Rico footprint and clinical operations).
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5 million) signed in Q2, the seventh straight quarter of four or more; two from new logos. Management said the large-deal run rate has moved from about 2-3 per quarter historically to 4 and wants to reach 5-6.
51 clients above US$5 million run rate, six more QoQ, the largest sequential addition on an organic basis in five quarters; 23 clients in the US$10 million-plus cohort after adding three.
Top 5 and top 10 client revenue share fell by 6 and 10 percentage points respectively over eight quarters; management says top clients are growing at industry rate.
More than 50% of revenues are non-linear; management is working to increase that share through productised services.
Management said renewals with some scope deflation have been held revenue-neutral by adding new work in adjacent processes.
Hedge book as of 30 September 2026: GBP 69.2 million at an average INR 116.6 per pound and USD 68.5 million at an average INR 95.7 per dollar over the next 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be affected by furloughs or holidays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business runs continuous mission-critical operations, so it does not expect the furloughs typical of IT services.

qa_highlights.question: Is attrition structurally higher than peers, and is it by design?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said attrition is not comparable to IT services; BPO-type operations are in line with industry averages. Voluntary attrition for associates with more than 180 days of tenure was 28.4% on a trailing 12-month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be stronger than H1 given the Q1 contract termination?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management cited large-deal ramps, the banking client transition, 17 new logos and a healthy pipeline; this is why the lower end of guidance was raised to 10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Has the healthcare vertical bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some timing issues, including the payer BPaaS wind-down and Medicare Advantage scope changes, are behind it. It cited HR1 provider-side tailwinds and voice AI and Denials AI now in production at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is needed to lift large-deal wins above four per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs more pipeline, proactive deal shaping and creative commercial constructs; it is pushing the sales organisation to reach five or six.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin trajectory expected to evolve beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 50-75 bps annual expansion toward 14%-15%, with levers including right-shoring, automation, pricing, exit of loss-making accounts, talent cost and facility optimisation; some gains are reinvested in capabilities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the lower guidance band 2% QoQ, and what drives the upper end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the floor reflects line of sight from H1 visibility, while the 13% upper end depends on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next two to three months.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI affecting deal sizes and decision cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-driven share-of-wallet expansion can lead to larger ACVs; Kairos intelligent context framework is attached to about 50% of the top 50 clients and has shortened some cycles, with one case going live in 8 weeks.

risks_watch: Healthcare sequential decline (-2% QoQ) continues after the payer BPaaS wind-down and Medicare Advantage scope changes; recovery depends on HR1 provider-side ramps from January 2027.
Recovery of the exceptional charge tied to two clients recognised last quarter is unresolved; management is 'optimistic' but gave no timeline.
H2 acceleration depends on phased transformation programmes hitting milestones and on pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months; the upper end of guidance is conditional.
Wage increments for senior staff in Q3 and continued onboarding ahead of revenue could pressure margins; quantified impact was not given.
AI-driven deal deflation and elongated decision cycles, which management says are offset by share-of-wallet gains.
Capitalisation of Kairos costs and the carrying value (INR 232 million under development) were not fully disclosed on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with clear reaffirmation of the margin path and a raised revenue floor. Cautious on healthcare and on the upper end of guidance, and evasive on Kairos capitalised costs and the exceptional-charge recovery, both of which were deferred offline.
key_quotes: Last quarter, I called this accountability.
We are actively engaged with them on recovery and we remain optimistic about the outcome.
Our answer rests on the intelligent context framework, part of the Kairos operating system, which gives AI the context it needs to work in a live operation.
AI does the heavy lifting, but a person signs off on anything that affects a customer or a regulator.
I wouldn't read anything into any aberrations on a quarter-by-quarter basis.
Kairos is not yet fully capitalized as a platform, but there are some costs which we need to capitalize.
So, the improvement that we are seeing is actually structural, it's broad-based, it's not driven by one single lever.

growth.why: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance raised at the floor to 10.5%-13% (midpoint 11.75%), backed by four large deals (two from new logos), 17 new logos and a banking client transition ramp, with H2 expected stronger than H1; no new physical capacity is being added and no capex-driven capacity is discussed.
